# Check 3: residual diagnostics

## One-step-ahead residuals for compositions

Pearson residuals of multinomial compositions are correlated across bins (they must add up), so their patterns can
mislead. **One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals** (Trijoulet et al. 2023) condition each bin on the bins before it; under
a correct model they are independent N(0, 1). `ss3_resid()` computes them for the SS3 likelihood: multinomial with
the adjusted sample size, or Dirichlet-multinomial with the precision implied by the SS3 effective sample size.
Growth curves by sex (`lhpar`) track cohorts.

```{r res-osa, fig.height = 5}
rl <- ss3_resid(ss3simple)                   # length; ss3_resid(ss3simple, "age") for ages
ss3plot_resid(rl, lhpar = lh)
ss3plot_resid(rl, type = "qq")
```

Pacific hake uses the Dirichlet-multinomial for its age compositions:

```{r res-phk, fig.height = 4}
data(ss3phk)
ss3plot_resid(ss3_resid(ss3phk, "age"), cohorts = FALSE)
```

## Conditional age-at-length

Conditional age-at-length data are a multinomial over ages for each length bin, so `ss3_resid(quant = "con")`
computes OSA residuals per length bin; `long = TRUE` keeps the bin for `ss3plot_caal()` (age by length bin, one
panel per year, with the growth curves by sex; with both sexes in one composition, females are circles to the left
and males triangles to the right of each age). Runs tests, joint residuals and hindcasts use the mean age by length
bin combined over the bins (`quant = "con"`), and `ss3_francis(quant = "con")` gives the Francis weight of
conditional age-at-length data as `r4ss::SSMethod.Cond.TA1.8()`.

The example is the GFCM benchmark assessment of European hake in the Adriatic Sea (GSAs 17-18; FAO GFCM 2024):
a two-sex Stock Synthesis model with eight fleets and three surveys, with conditional age-at-length data for the
Italian trawl (ITA_OTB_18) and longline (ITA_LLS_18) fleets in GSA 18.

```{r res-hke}
hke <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "hke.37.17-18", "hke.37.17-18.rds", package = "ss3diags2"))
lhh <- ss3_lhpar(hke)
```

The conditional age-at-length compositions are strongly down-weighted (SS3 variance adjustments 0.01 and 0.11),
so with the adjusted sample size most length bins hold less than one fish and give no residual. With
`nsamp = "input"` the residuals use the number of aged fish per length bin, with the Dirichlet-multinomial or
multinomial precision of the fit:

```{r res-hke-caal, fig.height = 6.5, fig.width = 10}
cl <- ss3_resid(hke, quant = "con", long = TRUE, nsamp = "input")
ss3plot_caal(cl, fleet = "ITA_OTB_18", years = 2018:2023, lhpar = lhh)
```

```{r res-hke-francis, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
fc <- ss3_francis(hke, "con")
fc
ss3plot_francis(fc)
ss3plot_runs(hke, quant = "con")
```

> **Reading conditional age-at-length residuals.** Each row of bubbles (one length bin) is one sample, conditioned
> from the youngest age up. Blue above and red below the growth curve means fish of a given length are older than
> the model expects (slower growth); a diagonal of one colour that moves one age per year is a year class.
>
> **Reading OSA residuals.** Bins are conditioned on the smaller bins: too few small fish gives negative residuals
> at small sizes and positive residuals at larger sizes. Diagonal patterns that follow the growth curves are year
> classes the model does not fit.

## Data weighting: Francis TA1.8

The Francis (2011) TA1.8 weight compares the observed mean length (or age) of each composition with its expected
value; with correct weighting the standardised residuals have variance 1. `ss3_francis()` gives the weight
$w = 1/\mathrm{var}(\mathrm{std.res})$ by fleet with a bootstrap interval and the new SS3 variance adjustment
(current adjustment times $w$), as `r4ss::SSMethod.TA1.8()`:

```{r res-francis, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
fw <- ss3_francis(ss3simple)
fw
ss3plot_francis(fw)
```

> **Check: data weighting.** $w < 1$: the compositions are overweighted relative to the variation of their mean
> lengths; multiply the variance adjustment of the fleet by $w$ and rerun. Wide intervals (few compositions) mean
> the weight is poorly determined. Dirichlet-multinomial fleets estimate their weight and need no tuning.

## Runs tests and joint residuals

The runs test checks the log residuals of each index (or the mean length or age) for randomness; the 3-sigma
limits come from the average moving range (Carvalho et al. 2021). North Atlantic shortfin mako:

```{r res-runs, fig.height = 5}
data(ss3sma)
ss3_runs(ss3sma)
ss3plot_runs(ss3sma)
```

```{r res-jres, fig.height = 4}
ss3plot_jres(ss3sma)
```

> **Check 3: residuals.** Red flags: a failed runs test (p < 0.05), residuals outside the 3-sigma limits, trends
> in the joint residuals (lowess line), RMSE above 30%. Actions: look for conflicts between indices, changes in
> catchability, selectivity or growth; never drop data only to pass a test.
